q2_flow.why: A dialogue that builds line by line is a small story that sets the craft up as the answer (K2, H5), and each step is a new picture every 2 to 4 s (R3, F8). After 0:08 the steps run wordless on screen (R3). At 16 s it is short and ends on the finished game (R2, R4).

q3_cta.what: None in the video. Caption: "אם בא לך את הקובץ תגיבי \"מקצוע\" והוא אצלך🎁".
q3_cta.why: One comment word for a real freebie, with a purpose (C3, R6, C2, C1). But it sits only in the caption, and nothing on screen asks at the end, right after the finished game is shown (C6). The word is generic and easy to type.

q4_shown.what: Top-down hands only (red nails, a ring): the finished tiles at 0:00, a printed sheet of profession pictures, glue stick, scissors, cut squares, pictures placed on magnetic tiles, then matching pairs. No child, face or price.
q4_shown.why: The finished game comes first and again at the end, so the result frames the process (H2, R4). Each step is done by hand, easy to copy (S4, F5). No child plays it, so there is no reaction (K8). The subject is a free printable, not something to buy (C7).

q5_edit.what: 5 shots in 16.3 s, 3.3 s average: a change at about 0:01, cuts at 8.2, 12.3, 13.3 and 15.4 s. Text builds line by line 0:00 to 0:06, gone at 0:08. No speed change. Ends on a hand removing a tile.
q5_edit.why: A change every 2 to 4 s suits a craft how-to (E2, R3). The text reads muted (T1) but disappears at 0:08, just when the steps get detailed (T2). No voice or sound cue explains the steps (E4). It ends soon after the result (E8).

q6_topic.what: A DIY matching game on magnetic tiles that teaches professions, opened by a child's question; free printable for a comment word. Serves a parent wanting a learning game.
q6_topic.why: A doable activity from everyday items, wrapped in a small parent-and-child story (K4, K2), is worth saving or sending to a parent (R7, R5). There is no occasion or buying moment, and the file is free (K7).

q7_filmed.what: Static top-down phone shots on a light table for the craft steps, then handheld close-ups for the sticking and matching. A woman's hands with red nails and a ring, bright indoor light. No face, no child.
q7_filmed.why: Top-down hands is the first-choice format (S4, F5), and the pictures fill the frame (F4). Bright tiles on a plain table pop on a phone (F7). Full 9:16 and sharp (F1, F3). The dialogue sits at about 25 to 40% down, inside the safe zone (T4, F2).

q8_text.on_screen: White bold dialogue with a dark shadow, centred at about 25 to 40% down, building line by line: the child's name then "אמא איך קוראים למכשיר שהרופא משתמש בו לבדוק אותנו?" (0:00), "אמא: \"את מתכוונת לסטטוסקופ?\"" (0:03), the child's "כן זה!" (0:05), "אמא: \"בואי הכנתי לנו משחק\"" (0:06). Gone from 0:08. No other text.
q8_text.caption: "סטטוסקופ? כן!🩺". About 35 words in four short lines: an echo of the dialogue, "דרך מתוקה וחוויתית ללמוד על בעלי מקצוע", a variant (memory or matching, not only on magnets), the comment-word offer, five hashtags.
q8_text.why: A short dialogue in the safe zone reads muted and opens on a real question (T1, T3, T4), but it lasts 8 s and leaves the detailed steps with no text (T2). The caption's first line echoes the hook, with five specific hashtags and topic words (T7). The word is easy to type (R6).

weak_points: No spoken or on-screen explanation after 0:08; the CTA only in the caption; no child plays the game; the child's name is in the on-screen text; the subject is a free printable, not a product; audio unclear.
lumebook_takeaway: Open on a parent-child line as text, flash the finished item, film each step top-down with hands only, and put the comment word on the last frame.
